title: Affine-Consistency Rejection Bound
statement: Let $n$ be a positive natural number, let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $p:\{0,1\}^n\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a proof table whose induced sign-valued function on $\mathbb F_2^n$ equals $f$. Let $w,w_0$ be Boolean strings of length $n$, and suppose that for every coordinate $i$, the local correction of $f$ in direction $e_i$ equals the sign encoded by $w_0(i)$ with probability at least $1/2$ under a uniform choice of the cube point. The affine-consistency tester samples a uniform coordinate and cube point, queries the corresponding input bit and the proof at that point and its translate by $e_i$, and accepts when the three encoded signs satisfy the affine consistency equation. Its rejection probability on the input formed from $w$ and $p$ is at least one half the relative Hamming distance between $w$ and $w_0$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on $\mathbb F_2^n$
The proof table is Boolean and has length $2^n$
The proof table induces the function $f$
$w$ and $w_0$ are Boolean strings of length $n$
Every coordinate's correction probability for $w_0(i)$ is at least $1/2$
